The paper considers high-order electromagnetic invisibility cloaks obtained by high-order transformations from general anisotropic media.
The paper proves that for any incident plane wave, at any frequency, the scattered wave is identically zero.
The paper proves that the scattering matrix is the identity, meaning the outgoing wave packet is the same as the incoming one for any incoming wave packet.
The paper shows that the cloaked objects are completely decoupled from the exterior, with electromagnetic waves unable to enter or leave the concealed regions.
The paper defines solutions with locally finite energy, requiring the electric and magnetic fields to be square integrable over any bounded subset of the domain.
The paper derives the cloaking boundary condition, where the tangential components of the electric and magnetic fields vanish at the outside of the boundary of the cloaked objects.
The paper assumes the permittivity and permeability in the cloaked objects are positive, Hermitian matrices that can have possible singularities only on the boundary.
The paper proves the self-adjoint extension of the Maxwell operator in the transformation medium is essentially self-adjoint and has no singular-continuous spectrum.
The paper shows the self-adjoint extension of the Maxwell operator in the transformation medium is unitarily equivalent to the generator of the homogeneous medium.
The complete decoupling of the cloaked objects from the exterior means the cloaking effect is undetectable in any scattering experiment with electromagnetic waves.
The paper generalizes previous results on first-order electromagnetic invisibility cloaks to high-order transformations from general anisotropic media.
The paper uses Von Neumann's method of self-adjoint extensions to rigorously analyze the mathematical problems posed by the singularities of the inverse permittivity and permeability.
The paper proves that it is possible to cloak objects inside general crystals, as the results are derived for media obtained by transformation from general anisotropic materials.
The paper assumes the media are not dispersive, which is a widely used idealization, but means the cloaking will only be approximate in practice due to dispersion effects.
The paper builds on previous work on electromagnetic invisibility cloaks based on the transformation approach, including first-order cloaks and cylindrical cloaks.
